page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AWS Graviton series ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, providing 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 48.0 GB of memory (6.0 GB per core), 7,500 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX and AVX-512, featuring hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions.

Benchmark results highlight a profile oriented toward balanced multithreading and I/O tasks rather than pure single-thread compute. The instance scores 12,134.02 in multi-core stress-ng tests and achieves 9.55 million Redis SET operations per second, both sitting in the middle 50% benchmark tier. Similarly, PassMark database operations record 5,248.2 and static web serving throughput measures 9.58 GB/sec. However, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 20.3 GB/sec. The ARM architecture also records low throughput on heavy machine learning tasks, delivering 35.79 tokens per second on text generation using a small 135M model and 6.76 tokens per second on a 7B model.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the is4gen.2xlarge provides strong resource density by packaging 7,500 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage with a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This makes it an effective deployment target for I/O-heavy applications that benefit from large local scratch disks or direct NVMe caching rather than paying premiums for external networked volumes. It is best configured for distributed databases, stream processing engines, log indexing clusters, and data processing ETL pipelines that rely heavily on local NVMe throughput rather than intensive single-core calculation.
